record.context_brief: Almost conjugate subgroups in compact Lie groups
record.original_question: Do the compact Lie groups SU(3), Sp(2) (equivalently Spin(5)), Sp(3), or G2 contain pairs of finite subgroups that are almost conjugate but not conjugate?

evidence.quote: Question 7.5. Are there almost conjugate and non-conjugate subgroups in SU(3) (resp. Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5), Sp(3) and G2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two subgroups $H_1$ and $H_2$ of a compact Lie group $G$ are called almost conjugate (or Gassmann equivalent) if there exists a bijection $\varphi : H_1 \to H_2$ such that for every $h \in H_1$, the element $\varphi(h)$ is conjugate to $h$ in $G$; equivalently, for every conjugacy class $C \subset G$ one has $|C \cap H_1| = |C \cap H_2|$. They are conjugate if there exists $g \in G$ with $g H_1 g^{-1} = H_2$.

Determine, for each of the compact Lie groups $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(5)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(3)$, and the exceptional group $G_2$, whether it contains a pair of finite subgroups that are almost conjugate but not conjugate.
